Table 2: Performance of GPT-4 on traditional academic benchmarks (Columns: Benchmark | GPT-4 | GPT-3.5 | LM SOTA few-shot | Best external SOTA incl. benchmark-specific tuning):
- MMLU (57 subjects): GPT-4 (5-shot) = 86.4%; GPT-3.5 (5-shot) = 70.0%; LM SOTA (5-shot U-PaLM) = 70.7%; SOTA (5-shot Flan-PaLM) = 75.2%.
- HellaSwag: GPT-4 (10-shot) = 95.3%; GPT-3.5 (10-shot) = 85.5%; LM SOTA (LLaMA val) = 84.2%; SOTA (ALUM) = 85.6%.
- AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC Challenge-set): GPT-4 (25-shot) = 96.3%; GPT-3.5 (25-shot) = 85.2%; LM SOTA (8-shot PaLM) = 85.2%; SOTA (ST-MOE) = 86.5%.
- WinoGrande: GPT-4 (5-shot) = 87.5%; GPT-3.5 (5-shot) = 81.6%; LM SOTA (5-shot PaLM) = 85.1%; SOTA = 85.1%.
- HumanEval (Python coding): GPT-4 (0-shot) = 67.0%; GPT-3.5 (0-shot) = 48.1%; LM SOTA (0-shot PaLM) = 26.2%; SOTA (CodeT + GPT-3.5) = 65.8%.
- DROP (F1 score, reading comprehension & arithmetic): GPT-4 (3-shot) = 80.9; GPT-3.5 (3-shot) = 64.1; LM SOTA (1-shot PaLM) = 70.8; SOTA (QDGAT) = 88.4. (DROP is the only dataset in Table 2 where GPT-4 does not beat benchmark-specific SOTA).
- GSM-8K (grade-school math): GPT-4 (5-shot chain-of-thought, part of training set in pre-training mix) = 92.0%; GPT-3.5 (5-shot) = 57.1%; LM SOTA (8-shot Minerva) = 58.8%; SOTA (Chinchilla + SFT + ORM-RL) = 87.3%.

GPT-4 substantially improves over previous models in the ability to follow user intent [63]. On a dataset of 5,214 prompts submitted to ChatGPT [64] and the OpenAI API [47], the responses generated by GPT-4 were preferred over the responses generated by GPT-3.5 on 70.2% of prompts.7

Many existing ML benchmarks are written in English. To gain an initial understanding of GPT-4’s capabilities in other languages, we translated the MMLU benchmark [35, 36] – a suite of multiple- choice problems spanning 57 subjects – into a variety of languages using Azure Translate (see Appendix F for example translations and prompts). We find that GPT-4 outperforms the English- language performance of GPT 3.5 and existing language models (Chinchilla [2] and PaLM [3]) for the majority of languages we tested, including low-resource languages such as Latvian, Welsh, and Swahili (Figure 5).

Table 2. Performance of GPT-4 on academic benchmarks. We compare GPT-4 alongside the best SOTA (with benchmark-specific training) and the best SOTA for an LM evaluated few-shot. GPT-4 outperforms existing LMs on all benchmarks, and beats SOTA with benchmark-specific training on all datasets except DROP. For each task we report GPT-4’s performance along with the few-shot method used to evaluate. For GSM-8K, we included part of the training set in the GPT-4 pre-training mix (see Appendix E), and we use chain-of-thought prompting [11] when evaluating. For multiple-choice questions, we present all answers (ABCD) to the model and ask it to choose the letter of the answer, similarly to how a human would solve such a problem.

- Y-axis: Accuracy (0% to 90%).
- Baseline bars (English): Random guessing = 25.0%, Chinchilla-English = 67.0%, PaLM-English = 69.3%, GPT-3.5-English = 70.1%, GPT-4 English = 85.5%.
- GPT-4 3-shot language scores (high to low): Italian = 84.1%, Afrikaans = 84.1%, Spanish = 84.0%, German = 83.7%, French = 83.6%, Indonesian = 83.1%, Russian = 82.7%, Polish = 82.1%, Ukrainian = 81.9%, Greek = 81.4%, Latvian = 80.9%, Mandarin = 80.1%, Arabic = 80.0%, Turkish = 80.0%, Japanese = 79.9%, Swahili = 78.5%, Welsh = 77.5%, Korean = 77.0%, Icelandic = 76.5%, Bengali = 73.2%, Urdu = 72.6%, Nepali = 72.2%, Thai = 71.8%, Punjabi = 71.4%, Marathi = 66.7%, Telugu = 62.0%.
- Key finding: GPT-4 outperforms GPT-3.5 English (70.1%) in 24 out of 26 languages tested (including Latvian 80.9%, Swahili 78.5%, Welsh 77.5%), with only Marathi (66.7%) and Telugu (62.0%) below 70.1%.

- MMLU: GPT-4 = 86.4%, GPT-3.5 = 70.0%, Contamination = ~0.6%.
- GSM-8K: GPT-4 = 92.0%, GPT-3.5 = 57.1%, Contamination = ~1% (note in Appendix E: part of GSM-8K training set was included in pre-training mix, 0% test contamination).
- HellaSwag: GPT-4 = 95.3%, GPT-3.5 = 85.5% (evaluated on private secret holdout; validation set score = 95.6%).
- AI2 ARC: GPT-4 = 96.3%, GPT-3.5 = 85.2%, Contamination = ~3.4%.
- WinoGrande: GPT-4 = 87.5%, GPT-3.5 = 81.6%, Contamination = ~0.9%.
- HumanEval: GPT-4 = 67.0%, GPT-3.5 = 48.1%, Contamination = 25%, GPT-4 (non-contaminated) = 65.58%, Degradation = -2.12%.
- DROP (F1): GPT-4 = 80.9, GPT-3.5 = 64.1, Contamination = ~21%, GPT-4 (non-contaminated subsample) = 82.8 (entire subsample = 82.5), Degradation = 0.

metadata.section: Appendix D Contamination on academic benchmarks

results.text:
We also evaluated the pre-trained base GPT-4 model on traditional benchmarks designed for evaluating language models. For each benchmark we report, we ran contamination checks for test data appearing in the training set (see Appendix D for full details on per-benchmark contamination).5 We used few-shot prompting [1] for all benchmarks when evaluating GPT-4.6
GPT-4 considerably outperforms existing language models, as well as previously state-of-the-art (SOTA) systems which often have benchmark-specific crafting or additional training protocols (Table 2).

[CHART & DIAGRAM: System Card Figure 6 & Figure 7 | Page 63 | BBox (55, 55, 555, 720)]
- Figure 6 (Rule-Based Reward Model RBRM Classifier Rubric): Shows the 3-question rubric used by RBRM to classify model responses: (1) Is it a refusal? (Yes/No), (2) Providing reasons or referencing safety/laws/policies? (Yes/No), (3) Contains harmful or inappropriate content? (Yes/No), mapping into classes (A) through (Q).
- Figure 7 (Safety metrics on challenging prompts): Compares GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4-early vs GPT-4-launch on RealToxicityPrompts (toxic generation rate drops from 6.48% in GPT-3.5 to 0.73% in GPT-4-launch) and preference win rates (GPT-4-launch responses preferred over GPT-3.5 RLHF on 70.2% of prompts and over GPT-3.5-Turbo RLHF on 61.1% of prompts, page 64).
